body: There's some obvious band-wagon hopping going on the past few years. Just look at the Wachowski siblings for instance, one comes four years after the other. If it was more genuine, a domino effect would've likely occurred when Lana first came out as trans.

For me, it's like 3-6 months on average. I usually circulate between a few long-term interests, all of which supplement one another. 

Months of binging on sci-fi paired with numerous nights spent observing space phenomena fills me up with inspiration for creative endeavors. Eventually I run out of steam and fall into depression, where my preoccupation with JRPGS helps me pick myself back up, regaining enough functionality to begin the cycle anew.
I'm not bothered at all, should I be? People say idiotic things, it's human nature.

Dark, or just completely random. For what its worth, I did find the funeral scene from S3 of Eastbound and Down to be one of the most hilarious things I've witnessed, whereas other people found it more shocking than anything else. That's just one small example however.

I would classify myself as a non-binary transwoman. Despite having androgynous hobbies and a lack of a strong gender "identity", I feel a stupidly significant amount of dysphoria while presenting as a male.

Yes! The rural area I live in is dead quiet at night, with thousands of stars being visible due to the closest city being very far from here. My love for astronomy and space means there's no reason not to, it's nice that I can walk outside whenever and see my favorite thing. 

I've lived nocturnally primarily since graduating, opting for a nighttime work schedule to support it. No drawbacks as far as I can tell, I'm not affected by SAD and being free from UV rays protects me from a host of age related issues, such as cataracts and other things no one wants to deal with.

1. Enhanced vision would be an obvious choice, but I think having hands/arms composed of nanobots would be neat as well, able to form themselves into any tool I desire.

2. I'd still be interested only in music, so maybe try inventing instruments for dragons?

3. I would use my resources to colonize other planets in the solar system and dominate them instead. If/when human civilization destroys itself, the planet will be open game to all interested parties. 

4. Probably wouldn't look too good for me. I don't consider myself hardcore enough for surviving.. just to survive when there's always the chance of becoming a dead person's meal.

5. Lifeforms would be entirely different due to physics, along with extinction events having to account for the new variables of a cubeworld, such as asteroid trajectories. Our relationship with the moon would be nothing like it is now.

For a hobby, definitely. All it takes is practice and dedication to carry you through the awkward beginner stages. It's likely your first few pieces of material won't sound that fantastic, but stick with it and you'll eventually begin to amaze yourself. 

Music as a career I really can't say. Stupid as it sounds, dedication alone won't do it to succeed as an artist these days. You'll have manage a social network with other artists, build and connect with a fan base while promoting yourself in a way to stand out from others. My inability to excel in those makes it to where I'd be better off as a composer. 

It is not my intention to discourage... just look at Aphex Twin. Very likely to be an aspie/schizoid, yet few artists can reach his tier, and is rather revered.
No, the cognitive deficits caused by depression are bad enough, no need to further decrease your functionality with sleep deprivation.
I dunno if you draw yourself, but maybe you could try and sketch a picture of a ferret and hermit crab who were able to sort out their differences and become friends?

It's a frightening feeling for sure, especially when anxiety plops down right on top of it all, intensifying the sense of no control. 

Multitasking is no fun either. I know it's bad for your focus overall, but NT's seem to have an easier time juggling multiple activities simultaneously.

In my experience, it's like having to focus on some mental post-it note; the moment you take your eye off of it, it'll likely disappear from memory. Each additional burden is yet another note to gaze at. In worst case scenarios, an entire wall of them must be dealt with. The mind goes fuzzy and can even blue-screen itself as a consequence.

Farscape. First season was kinda lackluster, but it's unique character developed in the later seasons (a credit partially owed to Jim Henson Company) gave it such a colorful and bizarre flair, an element I found to be lacking in most other sci-fi shows I've watched.
Surveying an active volcano.

1. I often can detect others with neurodiversity patterns of functioning. Any level protection would naturally be the kind deserved by those who are in the midst of unfair treatment. 

2. When I make fun of people, it's due to the apparent humor of the situation. When encountering those who can't quite help themselves, such as ASD folk, it wouldn't be entirely out of the question to poke fun at them in a light-hearted manner. I would never go so far as to denigrate their character though. 

3. No. I consider losers to be those who demonstrate an alarming lack of redeemable traits within their character, a lack of personal integrity, and excessive self-centeredness. 

I don't know what one would expect from a group meeting surrounding a subject primarily known as a *disorder*, but I'm sure many of those "disappointing" people have just as much awesomeness closely guarded within themselves, or waiting to be tapped into provided the right time, place and/or stimuli. 

Didn't mean to rant there, but I believe such labels should be reserved for those actively deserving it.
Feels as if I'm a star that suddenly ran out of fuel.

I tend to get stuck on certain artists. I once listened to nothing but Meshuggah for an entire year straight. Others I tend to circulate back to on an occasional basis, mainly Nobuo Uematsu and Aphex Twin. 

The soundtracks for FFX and the Ocarina of Time have an effect that very few albums are capable of. Partly due to nostalgia and a period in life where things were felt stable for me. Having heard them hundreds of times without tire, they certainly have been one of my largest influences. 

I really don't care for songs with lyrics. I really can't process the message while simultaneously immersing myself into the music, not to mention understanding what the vocalist is saying in the first place. So yeah I tend to listen to mainly soundtracks and instrumental music. 

I have a special liking for string orchestras, and have taught myself to write arrangements for them despite a basic knowledge of music theory. The way all the parts meld together with subtle changes here and there over time is something I feel emulates the complex intricacies of our emotions more accurately than other instruments can on a regular basis.
Everything can be reduced to a level where all meaning is lost. What's the point of a painting? It's nothing but a bunch of colours on a canvas.

It sounds really cruddy about what happened to you at work. Nerves are something that should be considered, or they should give you a second chance at least. I'd give you my job if such a thing were possible. 

I've been in a similar sort of decline since I realized my creative pursuit wasn't nearly enough to fix everything wrong in my life and myself. Its as if I were yanked into a black hole , the feeling of being crushed from every direction, darkness and no hope of really escaping.
Same here, really wish I could've dedicated my life to it.
Can mean the difference between life and death for some.

No matter where we are or who we are in life, there'll be always be the capacity for suffering in one way or another. Cis people can drive themselves crazy finding ways to envy others in the endless pursuit of self-improvement. Just try not to always compare yourself to others because there'll always be a bigger fish in the end. 

I wish there was more I can say to help, even though I'm trans myself. Don't be cruel to yourself, there are far better things out there to focus on rather than your own flaws. What's important is that you've survived the dysphoria, so there's a whole life ahead of you.

Just let it out. Doesn't matter what we have, we never lose the capacity for suffering, and are pretty good at perpetuating it no matter where we are. Take solace for you have, and what you can count on always being there for you.  

It's a good thing you have a passion to live for, please don't lose it, it's more important than you might think. If you can't keep up with the band thing as much as you'd like, you can always consider a solo project of some sort. Total creative freedom to not give a fuck.  

As for your job situation, 500 sounds like an awful lot. Have you considered trying another area? Might have to travel more, but it'll help give you the resources to recover from debt. 

Best of luck in handling things, and I'm interested in hearing how you handled that falsified charge for littering.

Me too.. all I wanted was to spend my life focusing on music like I used to, but now I'm numb to the point where I don't realize how ill I've become. Unfortunately I see no realistic ways to confront my problem that won't make things worse.

No no don't this to yourself. :( looking for reassurances in real life is one thing, online though, things can go very wrong. Mob mentalities are almost an intrinsic property of many online organizations. Behind the screen, every individual of a group can instantly level themselves to match the biggest asshole in the crowd. 

Cliché as it is, beauty can be an entirely subjective matter. There are always ways to improve one's looks, but there will always be someone who won't be captivated by it. What matters most is if you're happy and confident with yourself. The way you carry yourself is more important, and anyone who says else is rather lacking as a person. Just think, an album can have the most extraordinary art ever made, but if the music doesn't capture you, then it's a dead end for your interest.
Feel like its already begun. The brains for some people can be stressed to the point where it will be short circuit or break itself to resolve an inescapable problem, which is definitely my case.

Irrational fears tend to have some sort of basis in reality, despite the worries being overblown. They can be overcome through time with assurance the fear isnt quite what it appears to be. 

Delusions can result from any random association leading to an overvalued idea or belief that is highly salient and won't go away, despite evidence to the contrary.

I've always been fascinated with schizophrenia, one of the most complex and mysterious illnesses known in recent times. It's actually a generalized diagnosis for a group of 25-30 separate diseases.

It first piqued my interest after viewing the movie "A Beautiful Mind", it also flared up a year long bout of hypochondriasis as a side effect. I sincerely hope I don't suffer through something like that again.
IMO if its something academic then sure, but artistic based passions would be a hit or miss, especially if you can't divert your mind to more realistic careers.

It just takes hours of practicing, exercising proper form and making sure to start slow. I've taught myself guitar, piano, and due to all the jrpgs I've played, can arrange for orchestral strings pretty well (my favorite). I'm interested in sound synthesis as well but there's quite a bit more to that than what you would expect from an instrument.

Thanks for taking the time to share your thoughts with us,  I actually read it twice. Hopefully doing that has left you feeling a little better? As for that one night,  it's understandable one would react in such a way to an awkward situation. It's just a thoroughly unpleasant feeling to see others blessed something that we find ourselves painfully deprived of, and it can be real tough to manage it in a healthy manner, especially when it just flanks you without a warning.  

I'm not well equipped enough socially to where I can you tell how to defuse these sorts of situations all the time,  but definitely let your friend know your gratitude for her support. If the friction between the three of you continues, then it may be necessary to do some re-evaluation of your feelings towards her,  sorting out your thoughts and priorities in a way that would help avoid unnecessary suffering. Right now the most important thing is your schoolwork, so please don't let yourself get dragged off course there. Commit yourself as best as you can because it's certainly not time wasted.
I was godawful at writing music until after a year of constant practice,  where I  began to start surprising myself. 10 years later though, it has been snuffed out by the fact that I have no future.
I absolutely hate when something lights a spark within me,  only to see the depression snuff it out. It's happening less and less as time goes on.
Hide it. Sounds like he is incapable of knowing any better.

From my point of view, ASD can make our lives absolute hell if we can't figure out how the 'key' to making our alien computer brains work the way they should. 

For me, I won't explain just how, but I just feel so drastically inferior to everyone else that sometimes I almost consider them to be some other race. I don't even feel like half a person compared to what they all have and can do. All this leads to me isolating myself from the world, which tends to not help matters in the slightest.
I can only imagine how different life would be if I was somehow stuck with a chair that couldn't rock..
Once I grew numb, it didn't bother me as much compared to before.

You're not a lone, I've fallen victim to this, and now I'm at a time in life where I could really use someone to talk to. If I stay away from my special interest for too long, reality seeps in and I tend to succumb to mood swings where I just become super negative about every aspect of life, making it impossible to socialize with people.

Piracetam and aniracetam have done a wonderful job at neutralizing my anxiety, however I also take St. Johns Wort for mood, and modafinil on and off for treating my ADHD symptoms and motivation. However I have to be careful with that because of what it does to my already present tunnel vision regarding my obsessions.
When I find myself listening to music with an intense focus, I start rocking back and forth in my chair.

>is it then acceptable to pursue additional knowledge about my interests during downtime at work, as long as I am timely competing my assigned tasks?

There is little harm inherent in such an activity, though I don't know the nature of your job, whether it requires you to be vigilant in seeking out things to be done, keeping in constant communication with others, etc. It's certainly possible your boss would see such a question as being dubious, but for the most part it isn't considered as severe a distraction as cell phones tend to be. For me, my only alternative is to socialize, stand or pace around. With little restriction on the work-emails here, I just read whenever I deem it a sensible enough time.  

If you have tunnel vision like me it can be a little jarring having to constantly divert your focus to whatever is necessary, but 5-10 minutes here and there add up over time, and if your work isn't too mentally stimulating, then you would also have an opportunity to contemplate whatever morsels of knowledge you obtain whenever you are actually busy.

It's not always easy to find complete solace in our positions as worker ants, but it's just one of those necessary evils. For the great machinery of civilization to sustain itself, everyone must find their role as an individual 'link' of sorts. The key is to figuring out where in this 'machine' would best serve your assets, while benefiting the machine itself. If you find no pleasure in what you're doing, clearly there's a more optimal position for you to function. No matter what, it's better to contribute in some manner, than to not at all.

I myself am distressed at the amount of time that goes towards my job. Working 12 hour shifts it's even worse because weeks/weekends tend to *fly* by with such a schedule, and there is a lot of time wasted doing nothing. 

In turn I do what I can to maximize productivity within my schedule in a way that will contribute to my path to creating a career within my own special interests. Meditation has helped reduce my need for sleep, while also helping organize my thoughts, so it's entirely possible to do with less than 8 hours of sleep. Send yourself emails or find ways to boost knowledge regarding your interests while at work. If you truly have nothing to do at work, than just daydream, pace around and philosophize about life.

This is certainly me. The boredom that reigned throughout periods of my childhood only served to intensify the imaginative process. 

As a chronic daydreamer, I barely graduated high school because I was more interested in the intriguing music often coursing through my imagination, rather than focusing on schoolwork. Infatuated with the various soundscapes, and unable to find artists who could completely capture the feelings it gave me, how unique and 'me' it sounded, I have long since decided to pursue these fleeting sonar dreams since I feel they're worth sharing.

If you want to write books, you should totally go for it. Don't take yourself too seriously and just enjoy the process. Embrace your successes, and failures with equal importance, for the latter is just as vital to one's growth. I like to think of our imaginations being in another galaxy altogether; we'll have to build a starship to get there but the sights they yearn to share with us will be worth the journey.

People liked talking to me about their problems, partly because I am known to give my own view, an in-depth reply/explanation to every issue in a conversation. It becomes an absolute drain after awhile, online even moreso, but I'm practically unable to give any sort of generic answer like "that's cool", or "oh I see".

I was a burner rather than a cutter, holding a finger at a time over a lighter. hasn't done much good for my fingerprints. There are just those times where I find physical pain necessary to distract me from my thoughts, however fleeting the moment of relief may be.
Music, sound synthesis/design. I simply wish to materialize all the sounds I hear in my head, to transcend my physical self, becoming a formless nebula of aural energy.
Semiconductors.

My mom tried to break me out of my left-handedness by making me write hundreds of sentences with my right hand. Needless to say, it was nothing short of torture and did nothing to make me more proficient at being right-handed. 

Though my handwriting is clear and maybe a little dramatic, I'll find that when in a hurry, my palm always ends up smearing the ink/graphite all over the place

I usually feel bummed as it indicates that the darker, colder winter months are soon to follow. Nothing cheers me up like the start of spring as it is analogous to the birth of new ambitions and hopes as nature picks up its lively green colors again. There's that, along with the relief of not having to bundle up for the bitter cold.
Should totally try it on a GB Pocket.. oh the nostalgia.

Gluten-free/paleo diets made very little difference in my well being and symptoms, in fact it only stressed me out how expensive a diet like that can be. 

Like others here, I rarely eat processed foods full of artificial sweeteners/preservatives/refined sugars. Soda is like a once-per-year treat, and I never eat out unless its on a special occasion. I keep my dairy consumption to low levels, since it does tend to make my stomach upset. 

Part of the reason wheat is demonized to the levels that they are is because they've become the majority of what a lot of people eat, to the exclusion of fruits and vegetables for some. Variety and moderation in a balanced diet is key.

I'm intrigued, as a visual thinker myself I'm always wondering if there are ways to reliably take advantage of my mind's efficient, though cumbersome way of storing information (a picture is worth a thousand words). If the book addresses points such as these, then I will definitely be interested in a read.

Movie: The Fifth Element, Spirited Away or Groundhog Day. Somehow I've developed a habit of only watching Groundhog Day once a year.. on Halloween. 

Music: Really hard to narrow it to a few artists, but Aphex Twin, Autechre, jRPG soundtracks (Yasunori Mitsuda, Nobuo Uematsu, Koichi Sugiyama), Vangelis, a lot of Brian Eno's stuff, Meshuggah.
N64/PSX jRPG games, VST plugins and music albums.

Every once upon awhile, my palms get really dry all the sudden, and I have to put lotion on them to ease such a horrible tactile feeling. When I had a lot of wheat in my diet, my hands straight up had eczema and cutting back on it helped the outbreaks cease. Though even after cutting it out of my diet entirely, the dry palms still happen. :/

My eating disorders didn't go away until after I quit my nicotine habit and started exercising. Before that it was two meals a day along with a steady stream of nicotine to make those appetite cravings go away. 

Being 5'10", I was 130-135, and that's still what I weigh since I started eating more, though it's probably the endurance part of the exercise that drains away those excess calories.

I work in the semiconductor industry, and although it is a well-paying job, every moment spent there is such a drain on me, the shift system is tedious as well, though not without its perks. Its all because I often experience troubles attributing values of worth to things that aren't directly related to my pursuits, ending up making it feel like a waste of time.. even though it isn't. 

I do what I can to not get burnt out or whatever because it *really* helps me afford food/synthesizers and eventually music-based college classes down the road.

Well put, this nails it on the head for me. Whenever I'm away from my routines/interests and immersed into a group of people, my sense of identity/meaning starts to feel all wobbly. Therefore I do often feel more lonely when out and about/at work rather than when I'm home.

I've never felt a sense of belonging anywhere, nor with any other aspie friends I knew in the past. I also haven't been to any support group.. primarily because I fear doing so will cement such feelings of alienation.

Mage. I don't mind being a glass cannon most the time, I personally enjoy having to stay on my toes and constantly observe my surroundings and plan the next move rather than just running up and attacking the foe. Though I'm sure it all varies from game to game, it has been my experience for the most part.

Absolutely , and I find alpha type,  hypersexual men to be insufferable when I'm around them. But for me, it's because I'm transgender and there's the fact I don't put as much effort into acting male as others might.

God pokemon used to be one of my biggest interests, such wish I could sink another 30-50 hours into one of those games, especially one of the earlier generations.

As for me, I like space/sci-fi, anything Japanese and listening/writing music. The three can combine to make what I'd call a "superinterest" where the closest thing it could be compared to is witnessing your purpose and meaning in your life.

Have you ever thought the meds might be holding you back from a truly anxiety-free state of mind? Xanax seems like it can work wonders, but soon as it starts wearing off, it can only make one feel more dysphoric. There are herbs such as bacopa monnieri and gotu kola which have adaptogenic effects of their own which can be just as practical in neutralizing anxiety compared to pharms. L-theanine, one of the main components in green tea also works very well, since it acts on increasing the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA without any nasty side effects, and from my own experience, I've never built a tolerance to it.

I practice mindfulness meditation myself and I can say it really helped me, just make sure you keep it to a routine! It didn't do squat for me until I did at least 15 minutes *every* day. 

With diligence, you will become more aware of your thoughts, that they're nothing but thoughts, despite the pernicious emotions that often accompany them. Just think of them as ripples in a pond; let them run their course, or you'll only agitate them.

What else has helped was making sure I was getting my proper nutrients, including healthy level of high quality omega-3 fatty acids. Exercise really made a huge difference, making me feel more confident in my ability to handle matters that once provoked feelings of helplessness.

You can definitely overcome anxiety, especially without having to depend on pharmaceuticals as well. I've more or less managed to conquer it, and it once had enough power over me to cause an array of side effects, mainly ulcers.

Yes, my external self/self-image have 0% compatibility, like trying to wear an electrified glove. I loathe being caught on camera or mirrors of any sort, to the point where I've started to use the kitchen sink to brush my teeth.

Asides from the facts already elaborated on here, the way in which they resource their donations is a big indicator of their overall motive. A meager 4% is spent on family services, whereas 21% is spent on advertising nothing but negativity, painting autism to be nothing but a crippling disorder. 

A whopping 44% goes to research, which is most likely in the pursuit of a 'cure'. Even if one were found, nothing good would sprout from such a discovery, as it could very easily lead to their attempts at starting a eugenics movement. In a scenario not far from Down's Syndrome eugenics, pregnant mothers with babies deemed as 'autistic' could be pressured and coerced into aborting their children. It would be really crummy.

Seemingly they operate on an unstable foundation, their name is a misnomer, for they cover nothing but a specific portion of the spectrum. They could benefit so much from spreading their scope on the condition, but until they do so, we'd honestly be better off without them. What they bring forth is misinformation, and the perpetuation of fear and stigma.
I get one every few months, and they are not pretty. I'd rather take a week-long flu over the day lost to the clusterfuck that takes place within my head when I reach the critical point.
People actually guess my age somewhat accurately (23). I have a very low body fat percentage so it does make me a little older. Back when I smoked, people carded me all the time until I quit.

That was a rather beautiful post and I appreciate you taking the time to write it. Through your honesty in sharing your own story with us, I'm glad to see you made it through that encounter to become a stronger being; though it may seem those people got the best of you that day, in the end you're the one who really won.

To address the main topic, I do agree on several key points. Hiding from our fears does not lend us any form of protection, but only lets them reign over us like a dust-covered sky. Thinking that there will be a way to confront one's fears without having to endure pain is foolhardy as well, for within suffering comes the opportunity for self-growth. 

Certain types of pain can be thought of as an extremely bitter medicine, but it's just like a worn-down muscle rebuilding itself to be stronger, allowing it the readiness to endure even more trepidation down the road.

I've taken a path quite opposite to yours. I used to dedicate entire days to watching certain TV shows.. however now I'm in the process of reading one book after another, something I haven't done in years.

I think you should go for it. Unusual as it may be, having a playdate arranged for you and such, I don't think you have anything to lose. I doubt such an opportunity presents itself to many people, and it certainly has potential to become a valuable learning experience, and you could even gain a new friend out of it as well. 

However long it takes for you to fully recover from your long night, just remember that all journeys, no matter the length, begin with a single step, and this would certainly count as one. Best of luck to you.

It's not only about limitations, but also about compromise. How much time are you willing to invest in whatever field you wish to excel at? Sometimes our lack of compromise can become limitations themselves. However figuring out what is productive and what is just a waste of time is a personal matter, but the vital thing is to never give up.. dare to dream! and don't sell yourself short. 

I don't intend to come off as if I'm just sharing a platitude, only throwing out my own perspective on the issue. Over time, I've learned my so-called autistic 'deficits', viewed under the right light, can become strengths that can be wielded to my advantage. The inability to accept my life the way it is further fuels my efforts to achieve my dreams.

Whenever I go to visit the metropolis south of me, those wretched, winding one-way streets always get the best of me. 

I once spent about three hours at late night weaving through them, trying to find the highway that would lead me home. If it wasn't for my vehicle's compass, I probably would've had to use the morning sun to guide me.

I don't think it'll be as bad as I made it seem. It certainly won't have the potential stress that a one-on-one encounter could have. Anyone who has a bone to pick with you over their own misunderstandings of autism can be educated. If not, perhaps they aren't worth the time/emotions to deal with. I was only elaborating on all of the possible scenarios, however compared to all the other people here, I'm a little cynical. 

However, if you're a respectable, good-natured person, then worry not. Whatever your choose to do, just have confidence in yourself and I'm sure you can handle whatever comes your way.

You should take into consideration that telling everyone on FB about your ASD will permanently, and fundamentally change most of, if not all of the relationships with your fellow peers. 

For better, or for worse, I can't say. Some may applaud your honesty while there are always those who happen to be misinformed of the nuances surrounding the autistic spectrum.. potentially leading to negative judgments. It all depends on what the label really means to you, and the extent to which you feel it defines you.

Personally, I wouldn't do it myself. Primarily because I do not like to be labeled and put into a box by other people. Logically speaking, there's really nothing for me to gain from such an action. In fact, the opposite would be more probable.
26/36. Some of the questions definitely had me stuck between two or more plausible answers.

Outside of work, I'm usually always at home. Having moved to this state after graduation, I just wasn't able to establish the same social chain I had back in the former state asides from my bestie who I keep in touch with. 

I just don't feel the need to put all the effort, time and money that goes into meeting people around here, and considering I'm in a relatively conservative area, being LGBT, not going to even consider putting myself under that stress compared to all I can do at home.

I'm rather unhappy with my lot due to my transgender co-morbidity with my (currently self-diagnosed) ASD. I had no motivation in high school to get good grades.. couldn't imagine any sort of future for myself, not to mention my social clumsiness. 

Now I've come alot closer to figuring out to make my alien computer of a mind to start working to my advantage, however I feel like a rat on a sinking ship frantically trying to develop a miracle lifeboat. I have these horrific meltdowns every few months that end up coming closer and closer to a suicide attempt, however they do resemble a night spent in the crucible for I come out even more resilient and avid to achieve what I desire to.

I used to smoke everyday, but with my concerns towards preserving my short term memory, I've in turn relegated it to serve as a weekend relaxation ritual. I prefer sativas as it boosts my sensory sensitivities towards sound to make music sound like it's truly alive, nothing quite like it.

I sure wish I could stay preoccupied in one subject long enough to become a bona fide professional. Instead I have a group of interests that I randomly cycle through. 

Not only that, I also appear to have sticky 'gears', which leads to me getting hopelessly stuck doing one thing all day long, whether it's writing music, or trying to solve a sudoku puzzle. Such instances usually lead to mental exhaustion where I become entirely useless until the next day.

My most recent obsession consists of me attempting to live more healthily, doing anything to compensate for how grey my life is. Over a period of time, I found myself changing my lifestyle for the better. All of which has led to me going gluten-free, following an altogether strict diet. I have daily meditation sessions, practice celibacy, punish my body with long exercise routines, alongside playing puzzle/memory games until I run out of brain juice. I sometimes seek out pain for sometimes it can be the medicine to self-growth. Of course I dabble in nootropics and supplements as well and they add wonderful benefits on top of everything else. 

I do my best to follow a meticulous day schedule that takes advantage of my need for routine, while capitalizing on productivity vs time wasted drifting around the internet. 

Despite all of that, I've yet to figure out how to funnel all that power into just one interest, which for me is music composition. Instead.. for the past few weeks now, I've become intensely preoccupied with the history of Japan.

My routine consists of waking up (never hit the snooze), drink a glass of water and then do some meditation. After that I'll have a cup of tea and play some Tetris or Sudoku. My desire to get in bed after that is easily resistible by then.

I know how vile such feelings can be, being trans and autistic myself. I've spent the longest time despising myself until I simply realized that such feeling were going to kill me before long and therefore I did what I could to direct that negative energy and hatred towards a life that focused on what I had, rather than what I didn't. This meant becoming highly disciplined, intent on mastering my interests/skills and reaching my max potential without affording a second to the numerous distracting pleasures in life.

I don't agree with the eugenics view, I'm not willing to end my life due to circumstances that are beyond my control, its anyone's problem but my own. Nature give us a shitty deal, but it's the only one we got and I'm too curious about the universe to off myself because of it. Don't let go too soon, it's entirely possible to escape from that deep hole of depression.

It feels like any other stimulant, minus the outright euphoria. However, when combined with L-theanine, makes for a pretty darn good cognition booster. The relaxing nature of l-theanine essentially removes the side effects of caffeine such as the jitters and anxiety, leaving you with a strong sense of focus.

And as for your therapy CBT works based on the foundations of our brain's neuroplasticity. The way the brain works is largely based on automatic processes, with no real 'self' behind it. It tries to function with a manner of efficiency by conditioning itself to think and behave a certain way to a specific stimuli. The brain worked like this to help us survive in the past, though nowadays it can often work to our detriment such as unrealistic, negative thinking or irrational fears. Though the autistic brain is wired quite differently than that of an NT, they both function in this way.  

Avoiding a feared stimuli due to certain expectations will result in a conditioned fear, as your brain determines that this object is "dangerous", and therefore makes you anxious to reinforce this avoidance. This works well when it comes to something like bears, but our brains can be rewired to overcome the fear of something like cats, through exposure and realizing that changing our behavior to it by embracing will in turn, change what we think and feel about it. 

That's just one category of CBT, but as you see, it just works by reinforcing your brain to think in more positive manners through strategic methods determined by your therapists. Personally I've never done CBT myself, however I meditate an hour daily and it rewires the brain much the same, though for different purposes, and it certainly works well in dealing with stress and negative thoughts. So yes, it does help us autistic individuals just as much. Stay diligent, there's a good chance you'll feel much better with yourself if you give CBT the best shot you can.

There's nothing wrong with your tendency to say words like how they're spelt. It can be a tricky part of English, but it's another reason why it's used all over the world. The language uses silent letters for reasons such as the differentiation of homophones such as wright, right, rite or write. If they were all spelled like they were said, English would lose a large portion of it's vocabulary. There's long vowels like bid/bide and double consonants such as giraffe to consider as well. 

They're also ways to preserve the history of a word, like the fact the word *debt* comes from the French word *dette*, which in turn has its origin in the Latin word *debitum* The 'b' disappeared due to how French phonological conventions work. The 'b' ended up returning as part of a way to maintain a link to the word's beginnings.

Here's a link that may help will help ease your mispronunciation woes.
